extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry/number theory familiar with anabelian geometry, Frobenioids, and p-adic/Teichmüller techniques
extracted.subtask_description: Precise construction and structural description of Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters (systems of Frobenioids and associated base categories) from specified initial Θ-data, together with the definitions and properties of Θ-links, prime-strips, Frobenius-/étale-pictures, and related symmetry actions. Targets readers seeking formal definitions, hypotheses, and main theorems of IUT I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Θ-data (components and technical conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial Θ-data consists essentially of: an elliptic curve EF over a number field F; an algebraic closure F of F; a prime number l ≥ 5; a collection of valuations V of a certain subfield K ⊆ F; a field of moduli Fmod ⊆ F; a (nonempty) collection Vbad ⊆ Vmod of nonarchimedean valuations of odd residue characteristic over which EF has multiplicative (bad) reduction; and various compatibility conditions (e.g., F is Galois over Fmod, Gal(K/F) is isomorphic to a subgroup of GL2(Fl) containing SL2(Fl), EF has stable reduction at all nonarchimedean valuations of F, the inclusion Fmod ⊆ F ⊆ K induces a bijection V ↔ Vmod, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Definition 3.1 and the summary in §I1. The initial Θ-data determines the coverings C_K, X_K, cusps, and the relevant labelling and symmetry structures. Many constructions and uniqueness statements (e.g., determination up to K-isomorphism) depend on these hypotheses. The paper repeatedly uses this full package as the standing hypotheses for constructing Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime number l requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A prime number l ≥ 5 is fixed as part of the initial Θ-data; for diophantine applications l is taken to be “large” (roughly of order the square root of the height of EF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The finite field Fl and its decompositions (additive and multiplicative symmetries) play a central combinatorial role. Many constructions rely on l≥5; later diophantine estimates use l asymptotically large.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and role of V, Vmod, Vbad, Vgood
rubrics_metrics.description: V is a chosen collection of valuations of K inducing a bijection with Vmod (valuations of Fmod); Vbad ⊆ Vmod is a nonempty subset of nonarchimedean valuations of odd residue characteristic where EF has multiplicative reduction; Vgood (and V	ext{bad}) denote complements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The choice of the restricted set V (rather than all valuations) is essential: prime-strips are indexed by v ∈ V and are used to 'simulate' global multiplicative subspaces. Many constructions (e.g., local models of coverings, tempered vs. étale fundamental groups) depend on whether v ∈ Vbad or v ∈ Vgood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater (data and uniqueness of gluing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater (relative to given initial Θ-data) is a triple consisting of: (a) a Θ±ell-Hodge theater; (b) a ΘNF-Hodge theater; and (c) the (necessarily unique) gluing isomorphism between them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Definition 6.13 (i). Conceptually, a Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater is a system of Frobenioids thought of as a 'miniature model of conventional scheme theory'. The D-version (D-Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater) is defined analogously for the associated base categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: D-Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A D-Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater is a triple: (a) a D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater; (b) a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater; (c) the unique gluing isomorphism between them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Definition 6.13 (ii). The D-objects are the associated systems of base categories (Galois categories, prime-strips, etc.) used to encode the combinatorial/topological structure underlying the Frobenioid systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime-strip types and their local models
rubrics_metrics.description: Various prime-strip types (D, D(cid:4), F, F(cid:4), F(cid:4)×, F(cid:4)×μ, etc.) are defined; for each type, the portion labeled by v (especially for v ∈ Vbad vs v ∈ Vgood/Varc) is specified, e.g., D-prime-strip at v ∈ Vbad is given by the category equivalent to connected tempered coverings of X_v; D(cid:4)-prime-strip by the connected objects of the Galois category of finite étale coverings of X_v when v ∈ Vbad; F-prime-strip at v by monoids such as O^{(2)}_{F_v} with Gv-action; F(cid:4)-prime-strip models use units O^{×}_{F_v} equipped with Gv-action × q^{N}_v, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fig. I1.2 and the surrounding text summarize the list of prime-strip types and their models at v ∈ Vbad. The monoid models include rings of integers, unit groups, roots-of-unity submonoids, and q-parameters; Galois/tempered group actions are part of the data. Mono-analytic variants and global realified Frobenioids are also considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenioid notion and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: A Frobenioid (typically denoted F) is a category-theoretic abstraction of the category of line bundles or monoids of divisors over a base category D (a Galois/topos-like category). Frobenioids are used as the building blocks of Hodge theaters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See references to [FrdI], [FrdII]. The Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater is in essence a system of Frobenioids; constructions often involve associating Frobenioids to prime-strips or forming global/non-reified Frobenioids attached to Fmod or π1 of certain base D's (cf. Fig. 6.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: F(cid:3)±_l (additive/geometric) and F(cid:2)_l (multiplicative/arithmetic) symmetries
rubrics_metrics.description: The D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater is equipped with an F(cid:3)±_l symmetry (poly-action by F(cid:3)±_l on labels −l_2 < … < −1 < 0 < 1 < … < l_2 identified with elements of Fl), while the D-ΘNF-Hodge theater is equipped with an F(cid:2)_l symmetry (poly-action by F(cid:2)_l on labels 1 < … < l_2 identified with elements of F(cid:2)_l). These symmetries represent additive (geometric) vs multiplicative (arithmetic) combinatorial structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two symmetries play complementary roles: F(cid:3)±_l is suited to conjugate synchronization and Hodge-Arakelov-theoretic evaluation at torsion points; F(cid:2)_l is suited to descent to Fmod and constructions invariant under Galois permutations (e.g., reconstruction of Fmod). The gluing identifies certain labels (e.g., 0=±t ∈ Fl with j ∈ F(cid:2)_l).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of F(cid:4)-prime-strip_mod from q-parameters (Θ-link ingredients)
rubrics_metrics.description: By considering the 2l-th roots of the q-parameters q_v of EF at v ∈ Vbad and extending to other v ∈ V to satisfy the product formula, one constructs a natural F(cid:4)-prime-strip denoted F(cid:4)_mod associated to a Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This construction has an abstract, algorithmic formulation (Definitions 3.6(c); 5.2(iv)). It is one half of the Θ-link data: the other is constructed using the reciprocal of the l-th root of the Frobenioid-theoretic theta function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of F(cid:4)-prime-strip_tht from Frobenioid-theoretic theta
rubrics_metrics.description: By replacing the 2l-th roots of q-parameters with the reciprocal of the l-th root of the Frobenioid-theoretic theta function Θ_v (for v ∈ Vbad) and extending via the product formula, one obtains an F(cid:4)-prime-strip denoted F(cid:4)_tht associated to the Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the alternate, theta-function-based prime-strip construction; the Θ-link is the full poly-isomorphism between the F(cid:4)_tht of one theater and the F(cid:4)_mod of another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Θ-link (full poly-isomorphism between F(cid:4)-prime-strips)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters (relative to the same initial Θ-data), the Θ-link is the full poly-isomorphism (the collection of all isomorphisms) between their associated F(cid:4)-prime-strips (F(cid:4)_tht ∼→ F(cid:4)_mod).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Θ-link induces associated isomorphisms between F(cid:4)×-prime-strips and their D(cid:4)-variants (see Corollary 3.7 and [IUTchII] references). The Θ-link underlies the Frobenius-picture and is a key instrument for relating the Frobenioid-theoretic data of different Hodge theaters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenius-picture (chain of Θ-linked Hodge theaters and its non-permutation property)
rubrics_metrics.description: An infinite chain of distinct Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters indexed by Z and linked by Θ-links yields the Frobenius-picture: … → n−1 HT → n HT → n+1 HT → … . This Frobenius-picture fails to admit permutation automorphisms that swap adjacent indices n and n+1 while fixing the rest of Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Frobenius-picture formalizes an 'order-conscious' (Frobenius-like) structure; it induces chains of full poly-isomorphisms between associated D(cid:4)-prime-strips and exhibits a rigid sequential structure (see Corollary 3.8 and Fig. I1.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: D(cid:4)-prime-strip mono-analytic core invariant
rubrics_metrics.description: The D(cid:4)-prime-strip (denoted (−)D(cid:4)_>) arising from certain F-prime-strips may be regarded, up to isomorphism, as a mono-analytic core invariant of the Θ-linked Hodge theaters occurring in the Frobenius-picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Frobenius-picture induces an infinite chain of full poly-isomorphisms between these D(cid:4)-prime-strips; this mono-analytic core is stable under the chain (see Corollaries 4.12(ii); 6.10(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Étale-picture (canonical splittings compatible with permutations among spokes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Frobenius-picture admits canonical splittings (the ´etale-picture): an arrangement in which the relationships of the various D-Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters to the mono-analytic core are depicted as spokes compatible with arbitrary permutation symmetries among the spokes (labels n ∈ Z).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ´etale-picture formalizes an 'order-indifferent' (étale-like) structure and suggests that absolute anabelian reconstruction techniques applied to tempered and étale fundamental groups can algorithmically relate conventional scheme theory of different theaters (see Fig. I1.6 and Corollaries 4.12, 6.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and role of D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater as bookkeeping device
rubrics_metrics.description: A D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater is a bookkeeping device recording the action of the F(cid:3)±_l-symmetry on labels (−l_2 < … < −1 < 0 < 1 < … < l_2), with each label represented by a D-prime-strip (often equivalent to the Galois category of finite étale coverings of X_K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It encodes how labels (thought of as elements of Fl) are represented and permuted; used to track additive (geometric) combinatorial structure and to connect to tempered/étale fundamental groups (see §6 discussion and Fig. I1.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and role of D-ΘNF-Hodge theater as bookkeeping device
rubrics_metrics.description: A D-ΘNF-Hodge theater records the action of the F(cid:2)_l-symmetry on labels (1 < … < l_2), each label represented by a D-prime-strip (often equivalent to the Galois category of finite étale coverings of C_K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It encodes multiplicative (arithmetic) combinatorial structure and plays a role in descent to the field of moduli Fmod and constructions that require Galois invariance (see §4 and Fig. I1.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater by gluing Θ±ell and ΘNF pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: A Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater may be obtained by gluing a Θ±ell-Hodge theater to a ΘNF-Hodge theater along the identification of appropriate D-prime-strips so that certain labels (e.g., 0=±t ∈ Fl) are identified with corresponding labels j ∈ F(cid:2)_l.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gluing is detailed in Proposition 6.7, Remark 6.12.2, and Fig. 6.5; it is essential to recover the combined additive and multiplicative combinatorial structures of the theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial/algorithmic construction of important objects (†ζ’s, †ξ’s, †ζ/†ξ functoriality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key objects such as the †ζ’s and †ξ’s are constructed by functorial algorithms from the intrinsic structure of a D-Θ±ell- or D-ΘNF-Hodge theater (Propositions 4.7(iii); 6.5(i)-(iii)), rather than by comparison with a fixed reference model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This functoriality is crucial for later work (IUTchII, IUTchIII), particularly where independence of auxiliary reference models is required for combining with log-shell theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem B — characterization of profinite conjugates of tempered decomposition/inertia groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Let k be a mixed-characteristic nonarchimedean local field and X a hyperbolic curve over k. For the tempered fundamental group Πtp_X and the étale fundamental group (cid:10)Π_X (its profinite completion), every decomposition (resp. inertia) group in (cid:10)Π_X associated to a closed point or cusp of X is contained in Πtp_X iff it is a decomposition (resp. inertia) group in Πtp_X associated to such a point; moreover, a (cid:10)Π_X-conjugate of Πtp_X contains such a decomposition/inertia group iff it equals Πtp_X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This technical result (Corollary 2.5 / Theorem B) is used in developing Hodge-Arakelov-theoretic evaluation (IUTchII) and provides a new proof of normal terminality of Πtp_X in its profinite completion; assumptions of stable reduction may be removed by Proposition 2.4(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of Fl as finite approximation of Z and role of 'disentangling' additive/multiplicative structures
rubrics_metrics.description: When l is large, the arithmetic of Fl approximates Z; the decomposition of symmetries into additive (F(cid:3)±_l) and multiplicative (F(cid:2)_l) parts in a Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater is seen as a rough approximation to disentangling additive and multiplicative structures of Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This heuristic underlies the motivation for using Hodge theaters: to simulate 'global multiplicative subspaces' and canonical generators by working with restricted valuation collections and prime-strip labelling (see discussion around Remarks 6.12.3, 6.12.5).
